    <div>
      <h1>Vibe Coding Cliff Symptom Diagnostic</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A named, evidence-backed list of where this organization's own cliff is steepest &mdash; the input to deciding which repositories get context engineering first.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-01-vibe-coding-cliff-diagnostic</b><br>
      Pack B - Where we actually are<br>
      fill order <b>1</b> &middot; type <b>diagnostic</b><br>
      audience <b>eng-leader</b> &middot; Panel A of 4 &middot; one per team
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>The Agentic SDLC Thesis</b>, <i>The Vibe Coding Cliff</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch01-the-agentic-sdlc-thesis.qmd</code> L19-33 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch01-the-agentic-sdlc-thesis.html#sec-thesis-vibe-coding-cliff">#sec-thesis-vibe-coding-cliff</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    For each of the three failure modes, write down one concrete incident from your own codebase:
    the repository or module, how often it recurs, and the undocumented knowledge that would have
    prevented it. Then rate current pain. You need only memory and honesty &mdash; no telemetry and no
    repository access. "Across the codebase" is not an answer: name the module. If you have not hit
    one of the three, write <b>not observed</b> and say why. Column 6 carries the value forward, so it gets the most room.
  </div>
